name: Intermittent slowness in Vector US-EAST-1 region
text: We mitigated those conditions by reducing memory utilization on the impacted nodes, rebalancing affected workloads where needed, and increasing available headroom capacity across the region. All affected indexes should now be operating normally, and based on the mitigations applied, we do not expect this issue to recur. || A fix has been implemented and we are monitoring the results. Our team is actively investigating the root cause and working to restore normal performance.

name: Upstash Redis – intermittent connection issues in some regions
text: Connection health has since been restored and we've been monitoring the regions to confirm everything is stable. || A fix has been implemented and we are monitoring. || The issue has been identified and a fix is being implemented. || We identified intermittent connection issues affecting some regions. Fix is being deployed.

name: Temporary Database Routing Issue
text: Root Cause: During an ongoing migration to improve database routing reliability, a configuration step was applied inconsistently across regions. Resolution: Our monitoring alerted us within minutes, and the migration was promptly rolled back for the affected regions. Service definitions were restored, and normal database connectivity resumed by 15:08 UTC.

name: Increased Function Invocation Errors - ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND
text: Some deployments created between May 18, 2026, 06:15 PM - 10:16 PM UTC may have experienced increased ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND function invocation errors due to a bad rollout. Deployments created outside of this window are unaffected. The fix is being rolled out to existing deployments retrospectively and is expected to finish in the next few hours. || A fix is rolled out for the function invocation errors affecting React Router 7 deployments. To recover, redeploy your application or use Instant Rollback to a previous deployment from the dashboard. || We're continuing to work on rolling out a fix. In the mean time, customers may use Instant Rollback to a previous deployment version as an immediate workaround in order to recover. || The issue has been identified and a fix is being implemented. || We're investigating an issue where customers are currently experiencing application failures due to function invocation errors when using React Router 7.

name: Resolved: Elevated ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE errors in Vercel Functions
text: Those versions contain an upstream regression that breaks response streaming for node-fetch@2, which caused the errors https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/63989 We have resolved the issue by reverting to the previous Node.js version. text: By 16:21 UTC on April 14th, the issue was mitigated for the overwhelming majority of customers (~96%). name: Service disruption impacting the Dashboard, Webflow application and some form submissions
text: Our CEO, Linda, has shared a document that provides an overview of the incident that is available for review via the following link: https://webflow.com/blog/july-2025-webflow-availability-incident Additionally, our CTO, Allan, has prepared a technical breakdown of root causes, which also includes a breakdown of service disruption timing: https://webflow.com/blog/july-28-webflow-incident-report || Performance across all of our services remains stable. At the same time, our team remains focused on: - Expanding internal observability to provide more actionable insights to support root cause analysis - Offloading specific backend workloads to alternative resources, easing system load and improving overall performance New signups continue to be temporarily paused, and access to the Marketplace is unavailable. In parallel, our team is continuing work to: - Expand internal observability to provide more actionable insights that support the ongoing root cause analysis for our provider - Offlo
